title: Console, Layouts & Preferences
description: Filter console messages, customize and save layouts, and tune Editor preferences.

slides.title: Console Window 📜
slides.content:
# Messages, Warnings, Errors

The Console shows:
- **Log** (white) – Debug.Log() output.
- **Warning** (yellow) – Potential issues.
- **Error** (red) – Critical problems that may stop execution.

You can **filter** these using the three buttons at the top. **Clear** the console with the broom icon. Double‑click an error to jump to the script and line.

quizData.question: What color are warning messages in the Console?
quizData.explanation: Warnings are displayed in yellow to indicate non‑critical issues.

slides.title: Custom Layouts & Saving 💾
slides.content:
# Make Unity Yours

- Drag tabs around to create your perfect layout.
- Save it: **Layout dropdown (top right) → Save Layout**. Name it and it persists across projects.
- To restore default: **Layout → Default**.
- You can even **Delete** custom layouts you no longer need.

slides.title: Preferences ⚙️
slides.content:
# Tuning the Editor

Open **Edit → Preferences** (Windows) or **Unity → Preferences** (Mac). Here you can:
- Change **Colors** (play mode tint, background).
- Set **External Script Editor** (Visual Studio, VS Code).
- Adjust **Scene View** camera speed.
- Configure **Cache** locations and **UI Scaling**.

quizData.question: Saved layouts are only available for the current project.
quizData.explanation: Layouts are saved globally and can be used in any project.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Play Mode Tint

In Preferences → Colors, change **Playmode tint** to a very visible color (like bright red). It’s a strong reminder that you’re in Play mode!
